peg.peg_mechanism_score_basis: MEASURES HOW THE PEG IS DEFENDED, NOT THE CURRENT DEVIATION — which is why it can sit at 7.5 while the unit trades at 0.99988 (−1.2bp). Three-layer, battle-tested: USDC PSM 1:1, DAI parity, and CDP overcollateralization, with a clean ~20-month history. ⚠️ ITS STRENGTH AND ITS DEPENDENCY ARE THE SAME FACT: the mechanism is strong PRECISELY BECAUSE it is USDC-anchored through the PSM, so the peg defence and the concentration risk on Dependencies are two readings of one arrangement, NOT two independent findings. Do not treat a strong peg score here as offsetting the USDC concentration priced at axis 4 — that would count the same mechanism twice, once as comfort and once as risk.

backing.backing_score_basis: MEASURES RESERVE COMPOSITION AND ITS CONCENTRATION, plus the surplus buffer — NOT backing-over-supply. ⚠️⚠️ THE DISTINCTION IS NOT ACADEMIC HERE: RE-DIVIDING THE OPERANDS GIVES A NUMBER ON THE OTHER SIDE OF 100. Measured 2026-09-11 from the feed's own fields: total_backing $11,308,022,085.78 over supply $11,275,063,843.76 = 100.2923%, A SURPLUS OF $32,958,242.02. The PUBLISHED collateral_ratio is 99.4895% — A DEFICIT — because it is `100 + (surplus_deficit / supply)` with surplus_deficit −$57,557,885.05. ✅ That reconciles to the published 99.49 EXACTLY, which is what confirms the documented basis rather than assuming it. ⚠️ 80 BASIS POINTS APART AND OPPOSITE IN SIGN. A reader who divides backing by supply gets a surplus where the feed reports a deficit, and both are correct about different questions. ⚠️ Every USDS is minted 1:1 against a debt position, so par coverage is ~100% BY CONSTRUCTION and carries no information — the vow buffer is the signal. HELD AT 7.0: overcollateralized, diversified and on-chain transparent, well above opaque-CDP peers, held down by the ~33% USDC concentration.
backing.backing_score_persistence: filtered — reserve composition and buffer level, not a spot ratio
backing.backing_score_denominator: ⚠️ ASK WHAT THE RATIO DIVIDES BY BEFORE QUOTING IT. Published CR is surplus-based. To recover the backing-based figure: D' = backing − surplus. Quoting 99.49% as 'backed 99.5 cents on the dollar' is wrong in both magnitude and DIRECTION.

Measured from IlkRegistry.list() (35 ilks, $11,292,509,572 vat debt) against the same reading on 2026-08-01: Spark 21.66% -> 33.01% and has overtaken Grove, which fell 25.05% -> 15.34%. Obex flat to within $4M across both dates is the control establishing the readings are comparable. ~48.35% of the book now sits with two Stars scored a five-month-stale 7.0 (spark) and a provisional 6.0 (grove). ⚠️ A separately measured reflexive loop -- Spark holds $647,239,420 of sUSDS, Grove lends against sUSDS at up to 96.5% LLTV -- is RECORDED BUT DELIBERATELY NOT LOAD-BEARING for this cut, because whether published backing nets it out is not established. 6.5 stands either way.

liquidity.liquidity_score_basis: MEASURES CONVERTIBILITY CAPACITY AT PAR — the PSM and DAI rails — NOT executable DEX depth. ~$8.4B supply with 1:1 USDC PSM and 1:1 DAI convertibility, no KYC or geo-gate on the on-chain route, so the binding constraint under normal conditions is PSM inventory rather than slippage. ⚠️ THE DEPTH LADDER IS NOT THE RIGHT INSTRUMENT AND THE FEED SAYS SO: `two_pct_depth_status: not_size_responsive`, `two_pct_depth_size_responsive: false`, `total_2pct_depth_is_floor: true`. ⚠️ THE $50,000,000 IN total_2pct_depth IS A FLOOR FLAG, NOT A CLEARED RUNG — it is the largest size probed, not a depth that was tested and passed. Rendering it as depth beside this 8.5 shows a reader a tested number where none exists. ⚠️ AND THE EXIT INHERITS THE ANCHOR: convertibility at par runs THROUGH USDC, so this score measures a route that is only as good as the asset on the other side of the PSM — the same USDC dependency priced at axis 4, appearing here as an exit assumption rather than a reserve share.
liquidity.liquidity_score_persistence: filtered — convertibility rails and PSM capacity, not spot depth
liquidity.liquidity_score_depth_caveat: ⚠️ ANY 2% DEPTH BAND RENDERED BESIDE THIS SCORE IS A FLOOR, NOT A MEASUREMENT. The ladder is not size-responsive for this asset, so a crossing figure bounds nothing.

dependencies.underlying_score_basis: MEASURES CONCENTRATION OF THE COUNTERPARTY SET, NOT ITS QUALITY. ⚠️ AUTHORED 2026-09-06 — this axis did not exist on EITHER surface before that date, so there is no prior published figure it supersedes. Two concentrations, both real and both high-quality: (1) USDC is the single largest dependency at ~33% of backing, and it is the SAME name the peg mechanism depends on through the PSM — so peg strength and dependency concentration are one arrangement read twice, not two independent facts. The March 2023 precedent is the point: DAI followed USDC down through this module. (2) A less-transparent credit sleeve whose composition is drifting toward crypto lending and away from T-bills. Level with Backing deliberately: what this axis records is that the dependencies are CONCENTRATED, not that they are poor.
dependencies.underlying_score_persistence: filtered — supply architecture and reserve composition, not a daily balance

The axis was ANCHORED for the first time -- usds now declares dependency_protocols: ["spark","grove"], checked by scripts/check_dependency_protocols.py -- and could not hold 7.0 above grove's provisional 6.0 with spark five months stale and its economic_score explicitly flagged as never scored on its allocator mandate. axis-4 sets no mechanical bound; this is an authored judgement against two now-visible dependency scores.

issuer.issuer_score_basis: MEASURES THE ISSUER'S TRACK RECORD AND GOVERNANCE POSTURE, NOT THE ENFORCEABILITY OF ITS DELAY. Sky/MakerDAO is among DeFi's longest-track-record issuers — DAO-governed, broadly audited, $10M bounty. Docked for the upgradeable contract set and broad governance reach. ⚠️ THE 48h GSM IS CITED HERE AS GOVERNANCE POSTURE ONLY. Whether that delay actually protects a holder is priced on Contract & Admin, where it is measured and heavily qualified: no independent canceller (plot() and drop() answer to the same DSAuth authority), no MIN_DELAY constant so 48h is a setting rather than a floor, and a UsdsJoin path recorded at `timelock: none` that never enters the pause contract at all. ⚠️ DO NOT READ THE 48h IN THIS ROW AS AN INDEPENDENT MITIGANT — it is the same delay, and axis 5 owns the question of whether it binds.
issuer.issuer_score_persistence: filtered — governance and track record, not spot-responsive
